intro: VialGrade is becoming a research intelligence platform for peptide and biotech research. I want it to bring together lab reports, clinical trials, FDA records, papers, company information, and other public research data in one place, then use AI to help compare the evidence while keeping everything traceable back to the original source.
orientation: A friend of mine is really into biomedicine and peptide research, and that got me looking at the space. What stood out pretty quickly was how scattered the evidence was, because lab reports, trial records, regulatory information, papers, and company claims could all live in different places and be hard to compare.
origin: I started with COAs and batch records because they gave me a concrete way to work on the problem. Even when a document existed, I still had to figure out whether it actually matched the batch, company, or claim it was being used to support.

As I kept building it, the part that became more interesting to me was the broader research problem: how do you pull a lot of different evidence into one place, use AI to help go through it, and still make it obvious what came from where?
unknown: One thing I had to figure out early was what to do when the evidence was incomplete, because not finding a record doesn't automatically mean something is wrong. I would rather leave something unresolved or ungraded than have the software pretend it knows more than the sources actually support.
grading: The grading system was one of the first ways I tried to make that concrete. It can look at independent testing, regulatory records, and other documented evidence, but it still has to preserve uncertainty when the information isn't there or different sources conflict.
earlyUse: In an early update I had around 2,000 Google impressions, about 600 clicks into the site, and eight signups over a month, which honestly surprised me because it meant people I didn't know were finding something I'd built and actually using it.
takeaway: The direction I care about now is making VialGrade useful as a research tool: bring the evidence together, let AI help organize and compare it, and keep the source trail visible the whole time. It is for research and evidence review, not human consumption or treatment decisions.
researchDirection: The part I'm most interested in now is using AI to go through the research itself. I want it to be able to read a trial record, paper, FDA record, or lab report, pull out what changed, compare it against other sources, and point out where the evidence disagrees.
traceability: The important part is that the AI can't become the source. If it gives you a conclusion, I want you to be able to follow that conclusion back to the original record instead of just trusting a confident paragraph from the model.
